# Getting started

For a first real run, choose **Try working example** from the Overview or Workspaces menu. BuildSteer copies it into `~/Documents/BuildSteer Examples/hello-workspace` and opens it. Node.js 20+ is needed for its service and tests. Start its Notes web service manually, run the endpoint tests, inspect the JSON storage, and open the linked Spec Kit feature. The Blackbox Agent B packaged demo uses simulated results.

Open this repository in the BuildSteer desktop app. BuildSteer reads `productview.yaml` and opens the Overview.

The left navigation follows the product workflow:

- **Overview** summarizes the workspace; **Project Map** shows components and connections. Switch between Map, List and Source. Source displays the exact `productview.yaml` file read from the open repository, or the packaged YAML in the web demo. Add components from the map toolbar. Open **Files** for application source files.
- **Product** contains Backlog, Requirements and Documentation by default. Enable Vision, Roadmap and North Star under Settings → Preferences → Additional views when they are useful; the choice is saved in `workspace.additionalViews` in `productview.yaml`. **Run & Verify → Environment** shows required variable names and lets each developer set private values on their own Mac. Documentation browses all Markdown files in `product.docsRoot` with the same folder tree and reader layout as Requirements. Vision is a Markdown file; roadmap entries live in `productview.yaml`. Backlog saves local Markdown issues in `product.backlogRoot` (default `backlog/`) and shows optional GitHub or Linear source locations. Live synchronization is still planned.

When a repository uses GitHub Spec Kit, Requirements recognizes its feature folders and constitution. Select a feature to see FR/SC IDs, available artifacts, task and checklist progress, links to configured components and tests, and recorded test results. Refresh folders after external edits. A flat specifications folder remains a normal file browser. Add verified links in `views.specifications.links` when a feature should be tied to specific component and test IDs; `BUILDSTEER.md` documents the format.
- **Run & Verify** contains Services, MCP Explorer, Tests and Data Sources. Services can be started and stopped manually. Expand a test suite to inspect detected Node test files or discover Rust test names on request; run the full suite or one entry and open its recorded output. Other runners can list individual commands through `tests.cases` in `productview.yaml`. In Data Sources, click **Inspect source** to list PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB or SQLite tables, or local files. Select an entry for a limited, read-only preview. Set database connection URLs in local Environment values, never in YAML.
- **Activity** shows recorded workspace events, including test runs and agent connections.

The title-bar **Open** menu gives quick access to workspace, product, Run & Verify, and Activity views. It also opens the bottom event panel, which lists recorded workspace events. The file explorer opens beside the navigation on **Files** and closes when you switch to another page. Command-B opens Files or toggles the tree while you are there; Command-J toggles the event panel. Process output is available on the relevant service or command page. The sidebar button beside the macOS window controls expands or collapses the navigation.

Open **Settings** at the bottom of the sidebar for Preferences, Project & Connections, AI & Chat, and Agent Access. Preferences include System, Light and Dark appearance. **Additional views** lets you show **North Star** and **Command-line Tools** when you need them; both are hidden by default. North Star records one product outcome manually and shows its historical plot. Command-line Tools shows a readable manual for real CLI programs declared in the repository. The view switches are shared in `productview.yaml`; appearance stays on this computer. Project & Connections stores GitHub and Linear source locations in `productview.yaml`; credentials stay outside the repository. **AI & Chat** detects installed Codex CLI and Claude Code, lets you select one, and defaults to read-only inspection. Product Chat then uses the selected CLI with BuildSteer's MCP tools. Its microphone transcribes locally on macOS; review the text before sending. Agent Access shows the exact skill, schema, current YAML and MCP setup that a coding agent can read.

The desktop app saves product document edits, North Star definitions and manual measurements, roadmap changes and new map components in the repository. Review and commit these files with the code. Commands run only after an explicit click. Output and events are recorded in `.productview/`.

## MCP Explorer

Open **Run & Verify → MCP Explorer** to see project MCP servers found in `productview.yaml`, `.mcp.json`, Cursor or VS Code project settings. BuildSteer also includes its own read-only MCP server. Discovery reads configuration only. Use **Add MCP server** for a missed server or **Add to project YAML** to register a discovered one; each gets its own entry in `workspace.mcpServers`. You can remove YAML entries without deleting source files. Click **Connect** to start a local stdio server or contact an HTTP endpoint; multiple servers may remain connected, and **Disconnect** affects only the selected server. Inspect their advertised tools, resources, templates and prompts. Review a tool’s JSON arguments before **Run tool**. Use **Environment** to set a missing local variable. Static Bearer tokens work through `authEnv`; OAuth sign-in is not yet available. The last onboarding step asks you to check these findings.
